newsitem.title: USA: Jobs data show strong US economy-Labor Secy Herman.
newsitem.headline: Jobs data show strong US economy-Labor Secy Herman.

text.p: U.S. Labor Secretary Alexis Herman said Friday that the May jobs reports was good news for workers and reflected a strong U.S. economy.

"I think today's report ... is good news for the American economy and good news for the American worker," Herman told Reuters Financial Television. "To have unemployment again at 4.8 percent, the lowest it has been in 23 years, continues to tell us the economy is strong and creating jobs and those jobs are being created primarily in the private sector."
Herman said the current rate of jobs growth in the U.S. economy was sustainable and that she was not worried that it would spark a round of price increases.

"The outlook is very positive for us going forward," she said. Herman said the wage gains of American workers have been consistent and moderate at about 3.8 percent and she would like to see that continue.

"From the administration's perspective, we want to see unemployment go down and at the same time we want to continue to see the modest increases in wages that are occurring and make sure we keep the appropriate balance and not have inflationary pressures on the economy," Herman said.
She said as long as the picture remains consistent it does not pose a threat to the steady growth of the U.S. economy.
